audit.whatIsWrong: Two fabricated/misassigned ability names. (a) 'Crimson Rush' does not exist — Vladimir's Q is Transfusion and Crimson Pact is his passive. It appears in spikes[0].text and wants.you[1]. (b) 'Hemoplague (E)' is wrong — Hemoplague is his R (120s); his E is Tides of Blood (13/11/9/7/5s). It appears in mid and wants.foe[1], and whys[3] calls the same ability 'Hemoplague poke'.
audit.why: Riot Data Dragon: P Crimson Pact, Q Transfusion, W Sanguine Pool, E Tides of Blood, R Hemoplague. Tides of Blood is also charged at the cost of his own health and is blocked by enemy units — not a 'slow-moving orb', which the mid text describes.
audit.corrected: Use Transfusion for his Q sustain and Tides of Blood for his E poke; note it is minion-blockable, so standing behind the wave denies it outright.

audit.why: Sanguine Pool's untargetability (2s) dodging your Shadow Dash commit is already the focus of the page, and anti-heal is already called out in report[8] and breakdown.late — both flagged missing interactions are in fact present.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page states Sanguine Pool is 'on a 26-second cooldown' in both whys[3] and early.
audit.why: Riot's per-rank values are 28/25/22/19/16. 26 is not a rank value at any point; at rank 1 the real bait window is 28s, which is longer and materially changes the double-trade plan.
audit.corrected: 28 seconds at rank 1, dropping to 16 at rank 5.

audit.why: Both writable layers agree row by row (Skill/Shen/Shen/Skill/Skill/Shen/Shen) and the shape matches the data: Shen owns 2-3 once Shadow Dash and Spirit's Refuge assemble, it goes to Skill at 4-6 around the pool timer, and Vladimir's threat is late.
All four spikes present: Lvl 2-3, Lvl 6 (Stand United), 1st item, and Vladimir's 2+ item Rylai's/Shadowflame spike.

edits.before: Shadow Dash comes online — E into Vladimir before he can pool, Q through the blade while he is taunted, and your Ki Barrier absorbs his Crimson Rush Q return.
edits.after: Shadow Dash comes online — E into Vladimir before he can pool (28s at rank 1), Q through the blade while he is taunted, and Ki Barrier absorbs his Transfusion return.

edits.before: Use Spirit's Refuge to block his empowered Crimson Rush autos during the taunt window
edits.after: Use Spirit's Refuge to block his autos and Tides of Blood during the taunt window

edits.before: Vladimir's pool is on a 26-second cooldown and his Hemoplague poke is telegraphed — force two consecutive short trades to drain the pool, then win the third trade cleanly.
edits.after: Sanguine Pool is a 28-second cooldown at rank 1 and Tides of Blood costs him health — force two consecutive short trades to drain the pool, then win the third trade cleanly.

edits.before: Stack Hemoplague (E) poke and use Transfusion (Q) sustain to win the attrition game pre-6
edits.after: Charge Tides of Blood (E) poke and use Transfusion (Q) sustain to win attrition pre-6

edits.before: Levels 4 through 5 are a steady grind in your favour — Vladimir's Hemoplague (E) poke is his only real tool, so dodge the slow-moving orb with side-steps and punish the cooldown with a quick E-taunt. He cannot pool every trade; force two short trades in a row and his pool will be sitting on cooldown during the second one. At Level 6, Stand United changes the entire calculus: you can now safely give up the wave and TP-teleport to a scaling bot-lane fight, earning map gold and objectives that Vladimir's pool simply cannot contest globally.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 5 are a steady grind in your favour — Tides of Blood (E) costs him his own health to charge and is blocked by the minions in front of him, so stand behind the wave and punish its 13-second cooldown with a quick E-taunt. He cannot pool every trade; force two short trades in a row and Sanguine Pool (28s at rank 1) will still be down for the second one. At Level 6, Stand United changes the entire calculus: you can give up the wave entirely and swing a bot-lane fight, earning map gold and objectives that Vladimir's pool simply cannot contest globally.

edits.before: At Level 1 Vladimir is weak — no pool yet and his Transfusion Q has a long cooldown, so respect the first auto-exchange but do not give him free Q poke either; sit at the tip of your Q range and deny his CS. The moment you hit Level 2 and get Shadow Dash, the trade pattern flips: E into him before his pool (W) is available, activate Spirit's Refuge to block his retaliatory autos, and Q through the blade while he is taunted — Ki Barrier absorbs the Transfusion return and you come out ahead. At Level 3 the full loop is online; Vladimir's pool is still on a 26-second cooldown, so track it carefully and only commit your E when you know it is down.
edits.after: At Level 1 Vladimir is weak — no pool yet and Transfusion sits on a 9-second cooldown, so respect the first auto-exchange but do not give him free Q poke either; sit at the tip of your Q range and deny his CS. The moment you hit Level 2 and get Shadow Dash, the trade pattern flips: E into him before his pool (W) is available, activate Spirit's Refuge to block his retaliatory autos, and Q through the blade while he is taunted — Ki Barrier absorbs the Transfusion return and you come out ahead. At Level 3 the full loop is online; Vladimir's pool is still on a 28-second cooldown, so track it carefully and only commit your E when you know it is down.

notes: Both packet suspectNames were real hits this time: 'Crimson Rush' is fabricated (Q is Transfusion). The larger error the packet did NOT catch is 'Hemoplague (E)' — Hemoplague is Vladimir's R; the E is Tides of Blood. Sanguine Pool was also quoted at 26s in two places; the real rank-1 value is 28s.
